entities.label: Amos

scholarly.note: Often placed among the earliest writing prophets; core oracles usually dated to Jeroboam II’s reign.

entities.traditionalNote: Shepherd-prophet from Tekoa who preached judgment to the Northern Kingdom.
entities.bio: A shepherd and dresser of sycamore figs from Tekoa in Judah, called to prophesy against the Northern Kingdom.

entities.label: Hosea

scholarly.note: Many scholars see preaching rooted in Hosea’s day, with later editorial shaping of the book.

entities.traditionalNote: Prophet to the Northern Kingdom before the Assyrian conquest.
entities.bio: A prophet of the Northern Kingdom whose marriage became a living parable of Israel’s unfaithfulness and the Lord’s covenant love.
kings: Jeroboam II and later kings of Israel (to the fall of Samaria)

entities.label: Jonah

scholarly.note: The narrative setting is Assyrian Nineveh; many date the written book later as didactic literature.

entities.traditionalNote: Prophet sent to Nineveh; associated with the Northern Kingdom era.
entities.bio: Traditional association with a prophet from the Northern Kingdom; the book’s story sends him to Assyrian Nineveh.

entities.label: Isaiah

scholarly.note: Scholars often distinguish earlier Isaianic material from later sections reflecting exile and return.

entities.traditionalNote: Major prophet in Jerusalem during the Assyrian crisis.
entities.bio: Major prophet in Jerusalem during the Assyrian crisis, calling Judah to trust the Lord rather than political alliances.

entities.label: Micah

scholarly.note: Generally tied to the Assyrian period in Judah; some passages may reflect later editing.

entities.traditionalNote: Contemporary of Isaiah; preached justice and warned of judgment on Judah.
entities.bio: A Judean prophet from the countryside, contemporary with Isaiah, who denounced injustice and warned of coming judgment.

entities.label: Joel

scholarly.note: Dating is debated; many place Joel after the exile because of temple/community clues.

entities.traditionalNote: Calls Judah to repentance amid crisis; dating is less fixed than Hosea or Amos.
entities.bio: Calls Judah to repentance in the face of crisis (often linked with locust plague imagery) and looks toward the day of the Lord.
kings: Dating uncertain — often after the monarchy

entities.label: Fall of Samaria

scholarly.note: Assyria ends the Northern Kingdom; a fixed anchor for reading Hosea–Amos.

entities.traditionalNote: Assyria conquers the Northern Kingdom.
entities.bio: Assyria conquers the Northern Kingdom and ends its monarchy — a fixed anchor for reading Hosea, Amos, and related prophets.

entities.label: Nahum

scholarly.note: Oracles against Assyrian Nineveh, usually dated shortly before its destruction.

region.setting: Focus on Nineveh (Assyria); Judah hears the oracle

entities.traditionalNote: Proclaims judgment on Nineveh after Assyria’s long dominance.
entities.bio: Proclaims the downfall of Assyrian Nineveh after its long oppression of the region.
kings: Likely Josiah’s era in Judah; Nineveh falls 612 BC

entities.label: Habakkuk

scholarly.note: Usually set as Babylon rises; the prophet wrestles with why God uses a ruthless empire.

entities.traditionalNote: Questions God as Babylon threatens Judah.
entities.bio: Wrestles with God over injustice at home and the rise of Babylon as an instrument of judgment.

entities.label: Zephaniah

scholarly.note: Commonly linked to Josiah’s era in Judah before Jerusalem’s fall.

entities.traditionalNote: Warns of the day of the Lord in Judah before the exile.
entities.bio: Warns of the coming day of the Lord and calls Judah to seek humility before judgment falls.

entities.label: Jeremiah

scholarly.note: Core ministry spans Judah’s last decades; the book’s arrangement shows complex editorial history.

entities.traditionalNote: Prophet through Jerusalem’s fall and the early exile.
entities.bio: Priestly-line prophet who preached through Judah’s last decades, the fall of Jerusalem, and the early exile.

entities.label: Obadiah

scholarly.note: Short oracle against Edom; frequently linked to the trauma around 586 BC.

region.setting: Oracle against Edom; Judah’s crisis in view

entities.traditionalNote: Judgment on Edom in connection with Judah’s disaster.
entities.bio: Short prophecy against Edom for violence against Judah, often linked to the trauma around Jerusalem’s fall.
kings: Near the fall of Jerusalem (Zedekiah / early exile)

entities.label: Fall of Jerusalem

scholarly.note: Babylon destroys the temple and ends the Judahite monarchy—central timeline anchor.

entities.traditionalNote: Babylon conquers Jerusalem and destroys the temple.
entities.bio: Babylon destroys the temple and ends the Judahite monarchy — the central exile anchor for Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Lamentations.

entities.label: Ezekiel

scholarly.note: Exilic prophet among deportees in Babylonia; dated oracles are relatively clear.

entities.traditionalNote: Priest-prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
entities.bio: A priest-prophet among the exiles in Babylonia, known for vivid visions, temple themes, and hope of restoration.
kings: Exile under Nebuchadnezzar II (after Jehoiachin’s deportation)

entities.label: Daniel

scholarly.dateLabel: Setting exile; book often 2nd c. BC
scholarly.note: Court tales set in exile; many scholars date final form to the Hellenistic/Maccabean era.

entities.traditionalNote: Faithfulness in exile under Babylonian and Persian courts.
entities.bio: Court tales and visions of faithfulness in empire, set in the exile and early Persian period.
kings: Nebuchadnezzar II; later Babylonian and early Persian rulers (story setting)

entities.label: Return / temple rebuild

scholarly.note: Persian decree enables return; second temple dedicated around 515 BC.

entities.traditionalNote: Exiles return and rebuild the temple under Persian rule.
entities.bio: Persian policy allows Judeans to return and rebuild the temple, dedicated around 515 BC.

entities.label: Haggai

scholarly.note: Tightly dated to the temple-rebuild push under Darius I.

entities.traditionalNote: Urges the people to finish rebuilding the temple.
entities.bio: Urges the post-exilic community to finish rebuilding the Lord’s house.

entities.label: Zechariah

scholarly.dateLabel: Early oracles c. 520; later chapters debated
scholarly.note: Chapters 1–8 fit the rebuild era; later chapters are often dated later by scholars.

entities.traditionalNote: Visions encouraging the post-exilic community and temple work.
entities.bio: Visions encouraging temple work and hope for Jerusalem’s future under Persian rule.
kings: Darius I (Persia); governor Zerubbabel; priest Joshua

entities.label: Esther

scholarly.note: Story set in the Persian court; composition is often placed later in the Second Temple period.

entities.traditionalNote: Jewish deliverance in the Persian empire; origin of Purim.
entities.bio: Story of deliverance for Jews in the Persian empire, remembered in Purim.

entities.label: Ezra–Nehemiah

scholarly.note: Narrates reforms under Persian rule; final compilation may postdate the events.

entities.traditionalNote: Return, wall-building, and covenant renewal in Jerusalem.
entities.bio: Narrates returns, temple and wall restoration, and covenant renewal under Persian oversight.
kings: Artaxerxes I (and earlier Persian kings in the narrative)

entities.label: Malachi

scholarly.note: Usually placed after the temple is rebuilt, addressing covenant neglect.

entities.traditionalNote: Last of the traditional writing prophets in the Protestant OT order.
entities.bio: Confronts covenant neglect after the temple is rebuilt and calls the people back to faithful worship.
kings: Persian period (after temple rebuild; specific king not named)

entities.label: Tobit

scholarly.note: Diaspora tale set earlier; widely dated to the Hellenistic period.

region.origin: Northern exile setting in the tale

entities.traditionalNote: Not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me; in Catholic/Orthodox canons.
entities.bio: A diaspora tale of piety and providence; not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me.
kings: Story setting in the Assyrian exile era; book composed later

entities.label: Judith

scholarly.note: Historical romance set loosely in earlier empires; usually Hellenistic composition.

entities.traditionalNote: Not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me; in Catholic/Orthodox canons.
entities.bio: A Second Temple story of courage against an invading general; not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me.
kings: Story uses earlier-empire color; Hellenistic composition

entities.label: Wisdom of Solomon

scholarly.note: Greek wisdom text, commonly linked to Alexandrian Judaism.

entities.traditionalNote: Not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me; in Catholic/Orthodox canons.
entities.bio: Greek wisdom reflection on righteousness and idolatry; not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me.

entities.label: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus)

scholarly.note: Wisdom instruction from Jerusalem; Greek translation followed for diaspora use.

entities.traditionalNote: Not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me; in Catholic/Orthodox canons.
entities.bio: Wisdom instruction from a Jerusalem teacher (Ben Sira); not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me.

entities.label: Baruch

scholarly.note: Associated with Jeremiah’s scribe in setting; composition usually placed much later.

region.origin: Associated with Jeremiah’s circle in tradition

entities.traditionalNote: Not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me; in Catholic/Orthodox canons.
entities.bio: Writings linked to Baruch in tradition; not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me.

entities.label: Maccabean revolt

scholarly.note: Jewish revolt against Seleucid policies; frames 1–2 Maccabees.

entities.traditionalNote: Intertestamental crisis remembered in deuterocanonical histories (not in CFM’s Protestant OT).
entities.bio: Jewish revolt against Seleucid policies that frames 1–2 Maccabees and Hanukkah memory.
kings: Antiochus IV Epiphanes (Seleucid); Hasmonean leaders (Judas Maccabeus and successors)

entities.label: 1 Maccabees

scholarly.note: Prose history of the revolt; generally trusted for the political outline.

entities.traditionalNote: Not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me; in Catholic/Orthodox canons.
entities.bio: Prose history of the Maccabean revolt; not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me.
kings: Antiochus IV and successors; Hasmonean leaders

entities.label: 2 Maccabees

scholarly.note: Theological history overlapping 1 Maccabees, not a simple sequel.

entities.traditionalNote: Not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me; in Catholic/Orthodox canons.
entities.bio: Theological history overlapping the revolt era; not in the Protestant OT used by Come Follow Me.
kings: Seleucid rulers of the revolt period
